transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-27
Start time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Cara Nguyen (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Helm - Head of ML), Leo Ortiz (Helm - Platform), Anika Singh (Helm - Product), Samir Rao (Helm - Security)

Summary:
Maya and team are evaluating Redwood for a mixed-hosted/dedicated deployment; primary questions are around model selection (open models vs larger hosted models), context length (need up to 128k tokens for long-doc summarization), multilingual support (EN, ES, FR, PT, and occasional zh), and tool-calling (retrieval + DB writes). They want security guarantees (VPC, KMS, SOC2) and a small dedicated pilot to benchmark latency/cost for their workload.

Topics:
- Current infra and pain points
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs for model choices
- Context length and memory/KV cache considerations
- Multilingual quality and any fine-tuning/adapter options
- Tool-calling / function calling capabilities and restrictions
- Deployment modes: hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Next steps: pricing, security docs, benchmark schedule

Transcript:
[00:00] Cara: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — we have about 40 minutes, we're going to run through your use case and then talk model options and deployment. Maya, do you want to kick off with your goals?
[00:18] Maya: Yep, thanks. So short background — Helm builds a long-form document summarization product for enterprise legal and research teams. Right now we're running a mix of in-house models and API calls but costs are spiking and latency is inconsistent. Main requirements: long context up to ~100-128k tokens for some customers, multilingual outputs (English, Spanish, French, Portuguese, occasional Chinese), and ability to call external tools — particularly a retrieval service and then write results back to a DB. Security is also a blocker — SOC2, SSO, and KMS integration.
[00:42] Devon: Got it. When you say long context, is that for single-pass generation or chain-of-thought style where you might chunk?
[00:52] Maya: Mostly single-pass for a unified summary, though we do sometimes chunk and stitch. Ideally we want the model to be able to accept large context windows so we avoid complex stitching logic.
[01:10] Leo: On infra, we prefer not to route PHI through public hosted endpoints for certain customers; so we're considering Dedicated or Private for those accounts. For others, hosted is fine if we can get predictable latency and cost.
[01:28] Cara: That makes sense. From a model perspective we typically recommend a shortlist depending on constraints: for latency-sensitive and cost-conscious flows, smaller open models with quantization (e.g., Llama 2 13B Q4 variants or Mistral small-ish variants) in Dedicated can be good. For best-quality multilingual and long-context, we point to long-context variants or models specialized for extended context like the Llama 2 (long) forks or specialised long-context open models, or a hosted commercial model when quality matters and cost is less of a constraint.
[01:58] Anika: Can you call out tool-calling support? We need function-calling style outputs and also deterministic structured outputs for DB ingestion.
[02:10] Devon: Yes — Redwood supports function/tool calling and structured outputs. There are a few caveats: tool-calling is supported across model types but behavior can vary by model. For open models we add structured prompting and post-parse hooks; for hosted managed models we surface function-call primitives with stronger guardrails and streaming structured events.
[02:35] Samir: Security — we need KMS integration, audit logs, and VPC peering. Also, do you support HSM-backed keys?
[02:44] Devon: We have KMS integrations and can support HSM-backed flows in Private deployments. Dedicated supports customer-managed keys via KMS and audit logging. We'll share the SOC2 pack, and the VPC peering guide.
[02:58] Maya: Great. Back to models — can you recommend a short list for our use case with notes on context lengths and multilingual quality?
[03:08] Cara: Sure — initial shortlist: 1) Llama 2 70B (long context variants) — strong base quality, decent multilingual with instruction tuning, but heavy on infra; 2) Mistral-Instruct or Mistral large variants — good quality-per-cost, but context length depends on the specific fork; 3) Mixtral / Longform open models (emerging) that support extended context to 128k — good for single-pass summarization; 4) A hosted high-capacity endpoint (commercial) if you need best out-of-box multilingual quality and fewer infra ops.
[03:48] Leo: Do you have benchmarks for throughput/latency with 100k context?
[03:55] Devon: We have internal perf sweeps and can run a pilot benchmark with your prompt set. Realistic numbers depend heavily on sequence length and batching — at 100k tokens you'll see higher memory needs and longer per-request latency; Dedicated GPUs with tensor-slicing/kv-optimizations help, and quantized weights can reduce memory and cost but may slightly impact quality. We'll run experiments on 8x H100 or A100 pools depending on availability.
[04:26] Maya: On multilingual—we've seen varying quality with Llama 2; Spanish/Portuguese are usually OK, French borderline, Chinese poor. We may need to fine-tune or use adapters. Any guidance there?
[04:38] Devon: For multilingual gaps, options are: 1) adapter-based fine-tuning on curated bilingual datasets, which is light-weight; 2) using a larger multilingual base model; 3) hybrid approach — retrieval-augmented prompts with translated passages. We can recommend quantization + adapter recipes and help estimate costs.
[04:59] Anika: For function calling, we need reliable JSON outputs and backpressure handling in streaming — does Redwood provide structured streaming?
[05:08] Devon: Yes, we support streaming with chunked structured events. For some open models we do more post-processing, while hosted endpoints do native function-call streaming. We'll demo live in the benchmark.
[05:22] Cara: Quick Q about routing — you mentioned some customers want mixed deployment. We support routing policies so you can route sensitive customers to Dedicated/Private while keeping others on Hosted.
[05:33] Leo: That routing is critical. Also we'd like cost controls — per-route quotas and token-level cost visibility.
[05:40] Cara: Yep, Redwood Console has token breakdowns and per-route dashboards.
[05:46] Maya: What's the typical timeline for a Dedicated pilot?
[05:50] Cara: From contract to pilot usually 2-4 weeks depending on infra and VPC setup; if you want Private/on-prem it's longer. For Dedicated we can often provision a pilot pool faster.
[06:01] Samir: Any compliance implications running large-context models? For example, do we log full prompts by default? Need to know about redaction and retention.
[06:10] Devon: Logs are configurable; we can redact PII and provide retention policies. Audit logs for actions and API calls are available in Dedicated and Private. We'll include the retention and redaction options in the security pack.
[06:24] Maya: For the benchmark, what do you need from our side?
[06:28] Devon: A representative prompt set (including multilingual samples), a few example long docs (we can obfuscate PII), and target SLOs for latency and quality metrics. Also any exact DB/tool-calling schemas for function-call tests.
[06:43] Maya: We'll put together 10 sample docs and a 30 prompt set.
[06:47] Anika: On costs — curious how quantized 13B vs 70B compares in production dollars.
[06:53] Cara: Rough rule: quantized 13B on Dedicated can be 5-15x cheaper per token than a full 70B non-quantized run, but the quality delta varies. For multilingual long context, 13B may struggle; 70B (or hosted commercial) tends to give better raw quality. We'll provide ballpark cost estimates in the pricing doc.
[07:12] Leo: Does Redwood support mixed-precision and kernel-level tuning on Dedicated?
[07:17] Devon: Yes, our serving runtime picks optimized kernels and supports mixed-precision, continuous batching, and KV cache management. For long context we tune kernel selection based on sequence distribution.
[07:30] Maya: Any limitations for function-calling with open models around safety or hallucination?
[07:36] Devon: Hallucination mitigation is a mix of model selection, prompt engineering, retrieval augmentation, and guardrails in the runtime. We'll test accuracy on your benchmark and can suggest fallback policies — e.g., if confidence low, call retrieval or decline to write to DB until reviewed.
[07:55] Cara: Ok, let's talk concrete pilot steps: we'll send a Dedicated pilot proposal with pricing and a recommended model shortlist; Devon will share security docs and a VPC peering checklist; you (Maya) will share prompt set and sample docs; then we'll schedule a 2-hour benchmark next week.
[08:15] Maya: Sounds good. One more question — do you support sharded KV caches for stateful sessions across GPUs?
[08:23] Devon: Yes, KV cache sharding/replication is supported in Dedicated for very long-context streaming; it's a runtime config. We'll show configuration options in the benchmark.
[08:35] Anika: For multilingual evaluation, would you recommend fine-tuning or adapters first?
[08:40] Devon: Adapters are lower cost and faster; fine-tuning is heavier but can yield better domain adaptation. Start with adapters and retrieval augmentation; if that doesn't reach quality targets then consider fine-tuning.
[08:55] Samir: If we go Private/on-prem for some regulated customers, what changes?
[09:01] Cara: Private includes a customer-managed control plane, on-prem packaging, and HSM options. It requires more lead time and support engagement. We'll provide a separate SOW for Private.
[09:12] Maya: Ok, I'm fine starting with Dedicated pilot for a subset of customers and keeping hosted for low-risk tenants.
[09:18] Leo: For the pilot, can you also include an estimate for GPU hours and expected cost per 10k tokens with the selected models?
[09:27] Cara: We'll include those in the pricing; Devon will run example perf numbers once you share the prompt set.
[09:34] Devon: One note: when evaluating 100k-context models, we often recommend simulating production distribution (document lengths, concurrency) because peak memory is driven by worst-case sequence lengths.
[09:48] Maya: We'll try to capture that.
[09:52] Cara: Any other competitors you're evaluating?
[09:55] Maya: We're talking to OpenAI for hosted endpoints, and evaluating Anthropic and some self-hosted options via SageMaker and Hugging Face. The key differences for us are controlling cost and having predictable latency for long-context.
[10:08] Devon: Understood.
[10:12] Cara: Recap of next steps: 1) Cara send Dedicated pricing + contract outline; 2) Devon share SOC2/security pack + VPC peering guide + KMS/HSM notes; 3) Maya provide prompt set and doc samples; 4) schedule 2h benchmark (Devon + Maya). Any timeline constraints?
[10:30] Maya: We'd like the benchmark next week if possible; budget approval is by mid-May.
[10:36] Cara: We'll aim for the benchmark next Tue/Wed and get pricing over by end of this week.
[10:42] Leo: Thanks all.
[10:44] Cara: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and scheduling items.

End of transcript.

References shared: - Redwood Dedicated pilot deck (link shared in chat) - SOC2 + security pack (will be shared) - Benchmark worksheet (to be shared)
